description: Reported on a pad in T2 (and again on the first-turn roll-off, the Advance command re-roll and the charge roll): the tutorial's 'Exit Tutorial' escape hatch was injected into EVERY gameplay dialog, and on a controller it took the dialog away from the player. AcceptDialog.add_button() lands the button in the dialog's own button bar, which is a SEPARATE focus root from the dialog's content — so once focus was there, no D-pad direction could reach 'Roll the dice' — and InputDeviceManager's dialog watcher put focus there on popup, because its breadth-first scan hit the injected button before the content and '⚄  Roll the dice' did not match a confirm word through its leading glyph. This scenario pins the fix on the real deployment roll-off with the pad active: the dialog carries ONLY its own Roll button, pad focus lands on Roll, A rolls the dice, and the winner's Deploy First / Deploy Second screen walks under the D-pad. tut_exit_under_modal owns the other half — the hatch still appears once the lesson gate actually blocks the player.

steps.comment: pick up the pad on the MAIN MENU, before any dialog: an embedded Window is its own viewport, and SceneTree._call_input_pause filters _input by viewport, so once one is open no joypad event reaches PadRouter/InputDeviceManager at all. Claiming here is the only player path into a modal with the pad already active.
emit_pressed, not a real click: a real mouse event would hand the device back to KBM and the bug under test is pad-only
the boot must not have flipped the device back
the Formations panel is a modal embedded Window - synthetic root-viewport clicks cannot reach its controls (same escape hatch tut_t2_musterin_pad_formation uses)
THE FIX: nothing blocked the player, so no Exit Tutorial is injected into the roll-off
the dialog offers exactly its own action - no second, tutorial-owned button competing for the pad
pad focus lands on the dialog's action. Before the fix this read TutorialExitButton, because '⚄  Roll the dice' never matched the confirm words through its leading glyph
the card's own Exit is still genuinely unreachable under an exclusive modal, so it must not look pressable

steps.equals: A dialog is open — finish it first, then you can leave.
steps.comment: and the tooltip must not point at an in-dialog button that is not there
A on the pad = the focused Roll button. This is the press that used to hit Exit Tutorial.
the dice were actually rolled - the button bar has moved off the Roll screen (Continue / Deploy First+Second / Re-roll, depending on the roll)

seed 4242 hands this roll-off to the AI, so re-render the WINNER's screen directly to cover the second dialog the report named ('deploy first or deploy second'). Forced UI state, not a played-through one - the assertions below are about focus routing, which does not depend on how the screen was reached.
D-pad right — the press that used to do nothing at all, because focus was stuck in the dialog's button bar
D-pad left — and back again, so the player is not stranded on either choice
